title: Investigating Curved Strontium Sulfate Crystals Using Multimodal Microscopy and Spectroscopy
content: Many living organisms grow curved single crystals as skeletal elements. In nature, curving crystals often result from vesicle-templated crystal growth, biomolecule inclusions within the crystal lattice, or transient amorphous precursor phases. Typical examples are calcite spicules in sea urchin larvae [1]. While calcareous biominerals are most common in the biosphere, a few organisms mineralize earth alkaline sulfates. Notably, the endoskeletons in the marine protozoa Acantharia consist of single-crystalline strontium sulfate in a curved shape [2].
